tasks.title: Reserve scoped submissions before effects
tasks.goal: Establish durable pre-effect reservation and fixture-journal replay for the new machine submission path; real domain recovery and surface adapters follow in C.2/C.4.
steps: Add host-issued context/target/principal-scoped submission namespaces with epoch/expiry and atomic idempotency-key/request/plan reservations under the existing lifecycle lease.

Build one orchestrator admission service over an owner journal port: reserve an owner-selected run ID, durably initialize that same journal identity, mark journal-ready, and only then invoke a fixture effect once. Reconcile reservation-present/journal-absent with the same ID; refuse uncertain or conflicting journal state.
Same key/payload attaches to the retained fixture outcome, different payload refuses; retain compact tombstones and reject retired namespaces. Existing/Retired never dispatch.

Keep current default-lifecycle prelude untouched in C.1: its fresh run allocation creates scratch before reservation and prerequisite install can precede state journaling. C.2/C.4 own safe real-domain and adapter integration.
positive_cases: Concurrent identical fixture submissions produce one actual counted effect under the leased journal owner.
Lost fixture response followed by retry attaches to the same reserved run and retained fixture outcome.
negative_cases: Reservation-present/journal-absent resumes only the same run ID before effect; journal-uncertain, changed or missing-after-ready refuses.
Collected result or expired namespace permits an old key to rerun an uncertain operation; caller invents or renews a namespace.

tasks.title: Link short-lived operation owners to domain recovery
tasks.goal: Retain inspectable truthful outcomes across API exit, EOF and execution-owner crashes; add missing pre-effect owner journals for direct build, package and remote publication before those domains are protected machine submissions.
steps: Introduce operation handles that bind existing lifecycle/build/deploy/publication journals and retained terminal/partial results without duplicating their authority.
Advertise connection-loss policy; implement continue-to-completion or explicit safe-stop ownership and protected local attach/control for a still-running owner.
On owner crash recover from domain journals, preserving existing one-writer/one-parked limits and completed/pending/uncertain effects; do not synthesize success from EOF.

Adopt C.1 reservation/journal-ready fence for actual lifecycle, build, package, deploy and publication owners under the same domain run identity. Build/package artifact records and registry Published facts are post-effect evidence, not pre-effect operation journals; add missing owner journals and retained results before enabling their submits.

Advertise an operation as unavailable until its domain owner proves pre-effect identity, journal-ready, terminal/partial result retention and safe retry. Keep current one-writer/one-parked limits; no fixture or shape-only handler grants a real effect.
positive_cases: An operation remains inspectable after the originating API process exits.
A reconnect attaches to a live owner or receives exact recovery-required state.
A lost actual domain response attaches to the retained result or returns an explicit pending/uncertain recovery handle without a second effect.
negative_cases: Connection loss silently restarts a provider.
A second client bypasses the domain's existing execution limit.
A build/package artifact record or registry Published fact is accepted as an operation journal, or package is silently omitted from effectful machine coverage.

C.2 must keep the ordinary default-lifecycle path byte/behavior compatible while a separate machine path reserves a pure run ID, proves its matching lifecycle journal and ready marker, then permits scratch/prerequisite/provider effects. A matching lifecycle freshness header is not a terminal result; per-run owner-retained outcomes and cross-domain recovery remain separate work.

A lifecycle freshness header is not a terminal result. The lifecycle owner must retain a registered per-run marker and validated report payload (or typed unavailable partial evidence) under its own lease-pinned state, before replying. A displaced header without that owner record remains recovery-required; no result is copied into the reservation index.

Source audit found direct build/package apply before artifact records and remote publication before any local run journal; these are owner-journal implementation gaps, not evidence that C.1 protects them. Registry fact log is not a remote publication operation journal. All publication tests in this campaign use isolated fixture remotes; no next/1.1.0 public Git action.

A protected one-package local fixture needs a bounded no-follow package-tree witness before reservation and a recheck before the first install effect. The lifecycle process subtree is included for that witness and its tests; existing plan v2 bytes remain unchanged for Validate and empty Install, with any source-bound variant explicitly versioned.

A test-only orchestrator dev-dependency for an exact offline package-source fixture may update Cargo.lock; production orchestrator must not depend on vibe-package-source because that would cycle. Keep source-bound one-package admission test-only until the source factory contract binds served bytes to the pre-effect witness.

For the first fixed local-copy package, registry owns a bounded no-follow replay of its actual recipe-zero content hash over exact file paths/bytes. This may add vibe-safefs as a registry dependency; compare the independent result to fetched CachedPackage metadata before lock use. A mismatch may follow global cache insertion and remains uncertain. Do not substitute lifecycle's different tree-digest recipe.

A named local-only source factory may be added in the existing vibe-package-source owner using its builder/cells route; it passes through the unchanged orchestrator source port and must not create an orchestrator-to-package-source production dependency. Keep the host-admitted production entry unavailable until source-tree/root identity, recipe-zero content hash, cache partial effects and retained replay are bound together.

tasks.title: Multiplex progress, queries and cooperative controls
tasks.goal: Keep machine sessions responsive during long operations with bounded replay and honest cancellation.
steps: Separate request dispatch from long job execution and stream typed phase/state/progress/diagnostic events with per-stream sequence and context/target references.
Add flow control, bounded raw stdout/stderr and replay cursors; slow consumers receive explicit gaps/expired payload states without losing terminal result identity.

Implement cancellation-requested acknowledgement separately from reached safe stop; queries/control run while a job executes, and cancellation after committed effects returns partial/recovery outcomes.
positive_cases: A long fixture job permits concurrent query and cancellation requests.
Replayed events link to the same durable operation and final result.
negative_cases: Serial tools/call blocks all cancel handling.
Cancel acknowledgement is reported as rollback or an unlimited event queue accumulates.

tasks.title: Expose typed input and admission across all adapters
tasks.goal: Remove machine-mode TTY/prose decisions and fixed startup defaults that hide per-operation capability.
steps: Map domain NeedsSelection/input/approval requests to schemas bound to exact question, plan, scope and policy generation.
Carry explicit force/trace/deploy-profile and supported operation controls as validated requested options, preserving authority rather than silently choosing startup defaults.
Return structured phase and partial effects even when a handler exits without a final report; expose equivalent services through CLI, MCP and local API.
Route CLI, MCP and local API effectful submits through the C.1/C.2 reservation owner; retain equivalent idempotency and refusal semantics across surfaces.
positive_cases: A machine client resolves a typed selection and submits the exact resulting plan.
An authorization refusal includes scope and completed-effect truth.
Two surfaces racing the same scoped key invoke the domain owner once and observe the same operation identity.
negative_cases: Free prose or assume-yes is parsed as a blanket grant.
An Err after prior writes is serialized as no effects.
